query: After npm started resolving webpack 5.112.0, `ng serve` on my Angular 15 app that uses @angular-architects/module-federation fails during "Generating browser application bundles (phase: setup)" with "An unhandled exception occurred: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'tap')". Nothing in my code changed. What causes this and how do I fix it?
goldAnswer: Two webpack versions end up in one build, so make the project resolve a single webpack version, e.g. pin it with npm `overrides: { "webpack": "5.76.1" }` [Angular 15.2's build-angular creates the compiler with its pinned webpack 5.76.1, while the Module Federation config's `require("webpack")` loads the hoisted 5.112.0, whose ModuleFederationPlugin taps `compiler.hooks.validate` (since 5.106.0), which a 5.76.1 compiler doesn't have]

query: Gitea 28.x won't start on Windows Server 2012 R2: running gitea.exe just shows "This app can't run on your PC", while Gitea 1.27.x runs fine on the same server and the 28.x breaking changes don't mention Windows. Why, and what are my options?
goldAnswer: Gitea 28 is built with Go 1.27, which raised the minimum Windows version in the PE header from 6.1 to 10.0, so Windows refuses to load the binary on anything older than Windows 10 / Server 2016; stay on Gitea 1.27.x or upgrade the server OS [building 28 with Go 1.26 isn't an option because 28 requires Go 1.27]

query: After upgrading k3s from v1.35.6 to v1.35.7 (same on v1.36.3) on an old HA cluster that uses an external PostgreSQL datastore, the apiserver lists zero ServiceCIDRs although the row is in the kine table, and the PostStartHook "start-service-ip-repair-controllers" panics so the server crash-loops. What's wrong and how do I fix it?
goldAnswer: The old kine table's `name` column isn't using the C collation that newer kine's range-based list queries depend on, so listing misses the ServiceCIDR row; switch the column to the C collation, e.g. set `KINE_SCHEMA_MIGRATION=2` in the k3s service environment so kine applies its schema migrations [kine#693, released in kine v0.16.3, replaced LIKE prefix matching with greater-than/less-than range comparisons; this 2020-era database used the default en_US.UTF-8 collation; the migration runs `ALTER TABLE kine ALTER COLUMN name SET DATA TYPE TEXT COLLATE "C"`; stop all servers first and let one come up before the rest]

query:
Unable to find image 'mcr.microsoft.com/windows/server:ltsc2022' locally
docker: Error response from daemon: no matching manifest for windows(10.0.26200)/amd64/v3 in the manifest list entries: no match for platform in manifest: not found
goldAnswer: Docker's platform matching (its vendored containerd/platforms library) wrongly treats ltsc2022 (10.0.20348) images as incompatible with a Windows 11 25H2 host (build 26200); pass the platform explicitly with `--platform "windows(10.0.20348)/amd64"`, or upgrade to Docker Engine 29.8.0 or later [the library computed the compatibility floor wrongly for hosts newer than the latest LTSC (26100), which excluded 20348; the maintainer first guessed that 25H2 was missing from the compatibility list; 29.8.0 vendors containerd/platforms v1.0.0-rc.5 with the fix (containerd/platforms#34, moby#53427); seen with Docker 29.6.2 and the containerd image store]

query: After upgrading my Homebrew packages on Debian 12, every atuin run prints "ERROR: ld.so: object 'libgtk3-nocsd.so.0' from LD_PRELOAD cannot be preloaded (cannot open shared object file): ignored." even though the library is in /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu and ldd finds it. Why, and how do I fix it?
goldAnswer: Homebrew now uses its own glibc on this system and sets atuin's ELF interpreter (PT_INTERP) to Homebrew's ld.so, which doesn't search system library paths, so the bare library name in LD_PRELOAD can't be found; make the library visible to Homebrew's loader, e.g. symlink /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgtk3-nocsd.so.0 into /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/lib/ [the system became a Homebrew Tier 2 system (glibc 2.13 to 2.38), where Homebrew installs its own glibc; ldd traces with the system loader, which is why ldd still finds the library]

query: _tkinter.TclError: Cannot find a usable init.tcl in the following directories: C:/Programs/Python315/tcl/tcl9.0/init.tcl: version conflict for package "tcl": have 9.0.4, need exactly 9.0.3
goldAnswer: A stale `tcl\tcl9.0` directory left in the Python install folder by an earlier install or a manual Tcl/Tk workaround is being loaded; delete it, or uninstall, remove the install folder entirely and reinstall [a clean 3.15.0rc3 install has no tcl\tcl9.0 directory, and none of the 3.15 installers (a1 to rc3) ship one; the reporter also undid a renamed tk9.0 folder from an earlier workaround; deleting the directory and running Repair also works]

query: After building tmux 3.8 from source with GCC on a 32-bit ARM Linux box, the command prompt (prefix + :) garbles input: typing '-' shows '0' and a space shows '*'. Normal panes are fine, and 3.6b didn't do this. What's causing it?
goldAnswer: A GCC optimisation (wrong-code) bug that miscompiles tmux on 32-bit ARM, not a bug in tmux [GCC bug 122943, fixed in GCC 15.3: the space key (0x20) is misread as `KEYC_KP_STAR` (0x200000020); the reporter used GCC 15.2 with -Os, and a true -O0 build fixed it]
